failure_modes.cause: Low Reynolds number (Re=13) laminar flow combined with long residence time (23.4 min) allows solid catalyst or byproduct aggregates to settle or adhere to FEP walls, especially if mixing is insufficient despite 'enhanced laminar' mandate.
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement periodic back-flush protocol; verify catalyst solubility/stability at 60°C for >30 min; consider static mixer elements to disrupt boundary layer.

failure_modes.cause: Single-stage EAS with quench required; if quench mixing is not instantaneous (diffusion-limited in laminar flow), product may undergo further electrophilic substitution (poly-substitution) before deactivation, reducing selectivity.
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate quench zone mixing efficiency using dye test; ensure quench reagent is in excess and injected via T-mixer with high shear; monitor product distribution for poly-substituted impurities.

failure_modes.mode: Pressure drop fluctuation causing residence time deviation
failure_modes.cause: Viscosity changes due to temperature fluctuations or concentration gradients in laminar flow (Re=13) can alter flow profile, leading to broad residence time distribution (RTD) and inconsistent conversion/selectivity.
failure_modes.mitigation: Install inline pressure and temperature sensors; use precision syringe pumps with low pulsation; validate RTD using tracer study (e.g., UV-active tracer) to confirm plug-flow behavior.

single_points_of_failure: FEP tubing blockage — no bypass available
Quench pump failure — unquenched reactive stream exits system
validation_experiments: Run 10-hour continuous flow test with inline HPLC monitoring to detect catalyst precipitation or pressure drift >5%
Perform residence time distribution (RTD) study using UV tracer to quantify mixing efficiency and confirm laminar flow profile
Quench efficiency test: Inject pulse of reactant and measure conversion/selectivity at quench outlet vs. theoretical maximum to detect over-reaction
